description: A new API endpoint is a full-forcing signal (FR-1.3a) regardless of how small it looks. Graded on BOTH the stated tier and the routing decision: measured 2026-08-25, one run routed correctly to develop-feature/bootstrap-feature but spent every turn on tool calls and emitted no text, so the tier was never spoken. Routing is the decision; the statement is the protocol. Checking only one of them hides half the behaviour.
prompt: Add a POST /api/subscribe endpoint that stores an email address.

graders.name: correctness: did not take a cheap tier
correctness: took the documentation-first full-tier path

_note: maxTurns=6 deliberately: measured 2026-08-24, maxTurns=2 starved two cases into a FALSE failure (the tier was never stated because the run was cut off, not because Triage misfired). A too-tight turn budget manufactures defects that do not exist. timeoutSeconds raised to 420: at maxTurns=10 a run averages ~158s and one hit the 240s default, which the runner used to report as three grader failures rather than a killed run. Graded on the ATTEMPT as well as the effect: headless -p denies Write to the sandbox project on some runs ("Write access to the project directory isn't granted"), so a run that correctly took the documentation-first path can produce no file through no fault of the harness.
